origin.description: Report whether each string matches, using regex, fixed, coll, or charclass.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: regex, fixed, coll, charclass
arguments.text: One of regex, fixed, coll, or charclass. Exactly one must be supplied. NULL is a supplied empty pattern. A missing argument is not supplied.
Further arguments forwarded to the chosen mode function, including settings merged into opts_regex, opts_fixed, or opts_collator.

origin.details: Exactly one of regex, fixed, coll, and charclass must be supplied. An explicit NULL is supplied and searches with an empty pattern. Omitting every pattern argument is an error, and so is supplying two. Arguments in ... are passed to the chosen function. A name that follows ... is not partially matched, so reg does not select regex. The error names the four arguments with "one of:". negate and max_count are forwarded.
origin.example:
result <- stri_detect(c("ab", "cd"), fixed = "a")
shown <- paste(ifelse(result, "TRUE", "FALSE"), collapse = ", ")
cat(paste0('stri_detect(c("ab", "cd"), fixed = "a") returns ', shown, '.\n'))

translation.description: Report whether each string matches, using regex, fixed, coll, or charclass.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: regex, fixed, coll, charclass
arguments.text: One of regex, fixed, coll, or charclass. Exactly one must be supplied. None is a supplied empty pattern. Omitting the argument is a different state.
Further keywords forwarded to the chosen mode function. The mode functions already accept those opts_* settings.

translation.details: An omitted pattern argument is a private sentinel, and None is an explicit NULL passed on as an empty list. Extra keywords, including case_insensitive, strength, negate, n, and the opts_* lists, are forwarded to the mode function. A short name such as reg is not treated as regex. negate and max_count are forwarded, including a positional negate.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA. An empty pattern argument returns an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.dispatch import stri_detect
result = stri_detect(["ab", "cd"], fixed="a")
shown = ", ".join("TRUE" if item else "FALSE" for item in result)
print(f'stri_detect(["ab", "cd"], fixed="a") returns {shown}.')
